resources.string: 1. Install RemoteDesk on your Windows computer and run it.
2. A window with a QR code will open on the computer. If it didn’t, click the RemoteDesk icon next to the clock → “Connect phone…”.
3. Tap “Scan QR code” and point the camera at the screen. The phone and the computer must be on the same network (the same Wi-Fi).
Not connected yet. Tap to see how.
For safety, a computer is connected only with a QR code from its screen. On the computer, click the RemoteDesk icon next to the clock → “Connect phone…” and scan the code.
For advanced users: the QR code on the computer contains a link that starts with rdesk://pair. You can paste it here instead of scanning.
This is not a RemoteDesk code. Scan the QR code from the “Connect phone” window on the computer.
Pair this phone with “%1$s” (%2$s)? Connect only computers you trust.
The phone will delete its access key for this computer. To connect again, you will need to scan the QR code. You can also remove the phone on the computer: RemoteDesk icon → “Phones…”.
Adapters for turning on over the network (Wake-on-LAN)
Power and monitor buttons, files, clipboard and the screen are coming in the next versions.
Check that the computer is on, RemoteDesk is running on it, and the phone is on the same Wi-Fi network. If Windows asked about the firewall, allow access for RemoteDesk.
A computer with a different security key answered at this address. If RemoteDesk was reinstalled, connect the computer again with the QR code.
Each QR code works once. On the computer, click “Refresh code” and scan the new one.
The code is valid for 10 minutes. On the computer, click “Refresh code” and scan it again.
The computer has paused pairing for safety. Open “Connect phone” on the computer again.
This phone was removed from the list on the computer. Connect it again with the QR code.
The computer stopped responding in time. Check the Wi-Fi signal and try again.
The app and RemoteDesk on the computer are different versions. Update both to the latest version.
The computer answered something the app doesn’t understand. Try updating RemoteDesk.
The computer closed the connection: RemoteDesk was turned off, or the computer went to sleep.
Slide a finger to move the pointer. Tap to click, two fingers to scroll, tap with two fingers for a right click.
Whatever you type or dictate appears on the computer right away — in any keyboard layout, emoji included. The Send key on your keyboard is Enter.
Sticky keys — apply to the next key
All remote control settings will return to their defaults. Your computers and connections are not affected.
How far the pointer travels per finger movement
Pointer speed multiplier. Higher crosses the screen with less movement but is harder to aim. For a large or 4K monitor, try ×1.5–2. Default: ×1.
How much a page moves per two-finger swipe
How many mouse wheel clicks a two-finger swipe or the scroll strip produces. Higher scrolls faster. Default: ×1 (about one click per centimetre).
A tap on the touchpad is a left click
When off, you click only with the buttons below, and accidental touches won’t click things. Two-finger tap (right click) is turned off too. Default: on.
A light buzz on clicks and key presses
A short vibration on clicks, mouse buttons and keys, so you can feel that a press worked without looking at the phone. Also depends on the system “Touch feedback” setting. Default: on.
Height of the Left and Right buttons below the touchpad
Larger buttons are easier to find with your thumb; smaller ones leave more room for the touchpad. Default: medium.
Mirror the buttons and the scroll strip
The right mouse button moves to the left, the left one to the right, and the scroll strip to the left edge. The buttons on the computer itself are not swapped. Default: off.
The phone screen stays on while the remote is open
Handy for movies and presentations: the phone won’t fall asleep while you control the computer. Uses a bit more battery. As soon as you leave the remote, the screen turns off as usual. Default: on.
Fast finger movement sends the pointer further

Slow movement follows your finger precisely; fast movement speeds the pointer up to cross the screen in one swipe. 0% means constant speed. Windows may add its own acceleration (“Enhance pointer precision” in mouse settings). Default: 50%.
Finger down scrolls the page down, like a mouse wheel
By default scrolling works like a laptop touchpad or a phone: move your fingers up and the text moves up. Turn this on if you prefer the mouse wheel direction. Default: off.
Tap, then touch and slide to drag

Tap and touch again right away, then slide without lifting your finger — this drags windows and files. To tell it apart from a click, a single tap waits about a quarter of a second. Turn off for instant clicks: you can still drag by holding the Left button and sliding another finger. Default: on.
A Middle button between Left and Right
The middle button (pressing the wheel) opens links in a new tab and closes browser tabs. A three-finger tap does the same. Default: off.
A narrow strip at the touchpad edge for one-finger scrolling
Slide a finger up and down the strip to scroll, like a mouse wheel. Handy when holding the phone in one hand. Default: on.
The computer keeps running: music, downloads and games are not interrupted. The monitors wake up on touchpad or mouse movement or a key press on the PC.
The computer keeps running. The monitors wake up with the “Turn on monitors” button or a key on the PC keyboard. If the mouse gets bumped, the screen briefly flashes and turns off again.
A minute before shutting down, restarting or sleeping, a window with a Cancel button appears on the computer.
Windows politely asks programs to close. If something is unsaved, the program asks whether to save it and the computer waits for an answer — so it may never shut down if nobody is there.
Programs close without asking. Unsaved documents are lost — only use this if you are sure.
You can cancel the timer here in the app or on the computer — in the RemoteDesk icon menu.
Shut down, restart, sleep and sign out ask for confirmation

Before shutting down, restarting, sleeping, hibernating or signing out, the app asks if you are sure and lets you pick a time. Without confirmation the buttons work instantly — handy, but easy to mis-tap. Lock and monitors never ask. Default: on.
Wake monitors only with the button
An accidental mouse movement won’t turn the monitors back on

Normally, turned-off monitors wake up on any mouse movement — including bumping the mouse at night or sliding on the touchpad. With this setting only the “Turn on monitors” button in the app wakes them: if the mouse wakes them, the computer turns them off again half a second later (the screen briefly flashes). Any key on the computer keyboard always wakes them, so the computer stays usable without the phone. If the screen keeps waking up again and again (for example, the mouse jitters by itself), the mode turns off so the screen doesn’t keep flashing. Default: off.
“%1$s” didn’t answer within 2 minutes. If you’re away, that’s expected: the signal went over the internet, but the PC can be controlled only from your home network for now.
“%1$s” didn’t answer within 2 minutes. If it never turned on, open “About PC” → “Wake-on-LAN” and check the settings.
Couldn’t send the signal: the phone is offline. Turn on Wi-Fi — the same network as the computer.
Windows is ready: you can turn the computer on from the phone with the “Turn on” button on the home screen, the widget or the quick settings.
Something needs to be set up — open the wizard on the computer, it fixes things itself.

How to test: shut the computer down (Start → Shut down), wait 10 seconds and tap “Turn on” on the home screen. The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi. To turn the PC on when you’re away, enter your home internet address below.

Your home internet address — a dynamic DNS name (for example home.ddns.net) or a static IP. “Turn on” will send the signal there too. The router needs UDP port 9 forwarded to this computer and its IP bound to its MAC address.
Doesn’t look like an address. Example: home.ddns.net or 203.0.113.5
Only folders shared with the phone are shown. To add others or allow writing, on the PC: RemoteDesk icon → “Folders for phone…”.
This folder is read-only: you can download files but not upload or delete.
The file goes to the Windows Recycle Bin — it can be restored on the computer.
The computer is not responding. Check the connection and tap Refresh.
Recent — tap to copy to the phone; ⬆ to send to the PC
Text from the computer copied to the phone
Text sent to the computer’s clipboard
There is no text on the computer’s clipboard
There is no text on the phone’s clipboard — copy something first
The computer didn’t answer — try again
%1$s file(s) → “%2$s”. They are saved to the computer’s Downloads folder; if a name is taken, next to it with a number.
Connect a computer first: open RemoteDesk and scan the QR code.
